bioavailability.title: Bioavailability — from spray solution to target site

stages.label: Uptake / Translocation
stages.note: Illustrative source value; not a universal field efficiency.

stages.note: Illustrative source value; not a universal field efficiency.

items.name: Soluble Granules
advantages: Cheap packaging, easy transport, simple application equipment

items.name: Wettable Powder
items.mixing: Disperses in water to form a suspension; agitation/stirring is relevant.

items.name: Granules
items.mixing: Not presented as a conventional spray-tank dilution in the source table.

items.name: Water-dispersible Granules
items.mixing: Disperses in water to form a suspension.

items.name: Tablets
items.mixing: Source presents tablets as a convenient application format.

items.name: Soluble Concentrate
disadvantages: Soluble ai salts may have lower biological activity than their esters
items.mixing: Dissolves to form a clear solution.

items.name: Suspension Concentrate
items.mixing: Particles remain dispersed/suspended in the spray solution.

items.name: Emulsifiable Concentrate
advantages: High efficacy, low precipitation, little residue
items.mixing: The source states: active ingredient dissolved in oil becomes an emulsion in the spray tank.

items.name: Oil-in-water Emulsion (Emulsion concentrate)
items.mixing: The source states: active ingredient dissolved in oil in water is already a concentrated emulsion and is diluted in the spray tank.

items.name: Microemulsion
items.mixing: Presented as a water-based microemulsion with very small emulsion droplets.
